author: gdgassafda
quote: The hour has come to speak of this latest creation of the American machine. Grand Theft Auto Six has been released. The masses cheer. The critics call it a masterpiece. I call it what it is. It is a perfect portrait of a race in collapse. Look at the world they have built. Vice City. Leonida. A sun-drenched swamp of palm trees and neon and endless concrete. Every street crawls with the same mixture. The Negro. The Latin. The Oriental. The rootless white who has forgotten his blood. They rob. They murder. They chase money that vanishes the moment it is touched. This is not fantasy. This is the daily reality of the American cities that have abandoned hierarchy and blood. The two leads are a man and a woman bound by crime. They are not heroes. They are the natural product of a system that has destroyed the family and the nation. He is a broken soldier cast aside by the very state that used him. She is a criminal marked by the ankle bracelet of a justice system that no longer believes in justice. Together they steal and kill because that is all that remains when the higher purpose of race and soil has been erased. Struggle remains. But it is the struggle of rats in a sewer. The technical achievement is real. The streets live. The light falls correctly. The crowds move with the restless energy of a people who have no direction. That is precisely the point. The machine can render every drop of sweat and every reflection on wet asphalt. It cannot render honour. It cannot render the will of a people that knows itself. It can only render the chaos that follows when the Jew has done his work. For years the same forces have sold this poison under the name of entertainment. They dissolve the sense of hierarchy. They make the criminal the only figure who still acts with force. They turn the white youth into a spectator of his own replacement. Then they collect the money and call it art. The eternal pattern never changes. Finance and empty spectacle. Blood and soil reduced to background noise while the cameras linger on the next explosion. Democracy produced this. Internationalism produced this. The cult of comfort and silence produced this. A people that no longer believes it has the right to rule its own streets will eventually play games about ruling the streets of others. That is the true content of Grand Theft Auto Six. It is not rebellion. It is confession. The struggle continues. The race that forgets this law will be swept away by those who still remember it. This game is only a symptom. The disease is older and deeper. Those who still possess the will to see must look past the glowing screens and recognize the hour.
